surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $917 million, above the preview’s estimated $900–910 million buy-side bar, as well as the company guidance ceiling. This was a positive but not enormous beat against the preview’s elevated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue of $917 million grew 13% year-over-year and exceeded the top of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume the buy-side bar is ~$900–910M”; the preview also projected a Q4 pattern of “$905–915M.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $4.42 fell well short of the preview’s expected $4.80-plus whisper level, even though it was above the published consensus estimate. The gap was substantial against the preview’s stated buy-side bar.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the pattern implied “$4.85–4.95” and to “assume the buy-side bar is … ~$4.80+.”

surprises.description: FY26 revenue reached $3.4 billion, exceeding the preview’s $3.37–3.39 billion estimate and the company’s 9–10% growth guidance, with actual growth at 11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 revenue reached $3.4 billion (up 11%, with 19% product growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue consensus of “~$3.37–3.39B” and company guidance of “+9–10%.”

surprises.description: Software revenue grew 19% in Q4, a stronger result than the preview’s recent-trend concern that another mid-single-digit quarter could undermine the FY27 reacceleration case. The preview identified a double-digit Q4 print as the threshold that would de-risk that outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Software revenue rose 19% to $271 million in Q4,” with FY27 guidance for “solid double-digit software growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A double-digit Q4 print de-risks the FY27 software reacceleration claim” and warned that “another mid-single-digit quarter” would make it an “act of faith.”

surprises.description: F5 raised the FY27 hardware-growth outlook beyond the preview’s expected mid-single-digit growth for the next few years: systems guidance is upper-single-digit, although weighted toward the first half. Q4 systems growth remained strong at 29%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Systems revenue rose 29% to $239 million”; FY27 guidance is for “upper-single-digit systems growth (front-half weighted).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had framed “hardware growing mid-single digits for the next few years” and flagged a possible post-FY26 hardware air pocket.

surprises.description: FY27 gross-margin guidance of 80.5–82.5% implies a decline from Q4’s 84%, with management citing higher memory and component costs. The preview emphasized preserving a 35%+ operating margin as an upside lever; the 33–35% operating-margin range does not clearly preserve that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 80.5%-82.5%, down from Q4's 84%, reflecting higher memory and component costs, with non-GAAP operating margin of 33%-35%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “a guide that preserves 35%+ operating margin is an under-appreciated upside lever” and cited Q3 non-GAAP operating margin of 35.0%.

surprises.description: AI demand was quantified at a much larger scale than the preview’s existing $50 million cumulative disclosure: FY26 direct AI-use-case bookings exceeded $100 million and nearly tripled year over year, while active AI customers quadrupled to more than 200. The preview had identified a larger AI disclosure as a potential catalyst but did not anticipate these figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct AI use case bookings more than doubled to over $100 million in FY26 (up nearly 300% year-over-year) and active AI customers grew 4x to more than 200.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said AI-attributed revenue had “crossed $50M cumulative in Q3” and that “a new, larger disclosure” was a likely bull catalyst.

surprises.description: Regional growth was sharply uneven: EMEA and APAC grew much faster than the Americas, an unexpected source of strength in the reported results. The call attributed the outperformance largely to digital sovereignty and hybrid multi-cloud adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA grew 31% and APAC grew 14% in Q4, substantially outpacing the Americas at 5%, driven largely by digital sovereignty and hybrid multi-cloud adoption.”

surprises.description: The buyback refresh was larger than the preview’s stated remaining authorization: the Board authorized another $1.5 billion, bringing total authorization to $1.8 billion, while the company committed to returning at least 50% of FY27 free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F5 repurchased $600 million of stock in FY26 and the Board authorized an additional $1.5 billion (bringing total authorization to $1.8 billion), with a commitment to return at least 50% of annual free cash flow in FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$422M authorization remaining at Q3,” a target of “≥50% of FCF,” and said a refreshed authorization was plausible.

surprises.description: SaaS and Managed Services ARR ended FY26 at $211 million, with core ARR growing 24%, and management positioned the now-complete legacy transition as setting up a new FY27 growth driver. The preview expected the transition to be complete but did not provide an ARR estimate or this growth framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS and Managed Services ARR ended FY26 at $211 million (up 14%, with core ARR up 24%), and with the legacy transition now complete, this ratable business is positioned to become a new growth driver in FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated “legacy SaaS transitions complete” and flagged services growth as a forward indicator, but gave no ARR figure.

surprises.description: F5 disclosed meaningful security growth and rapid uptake of AI-powered WAF: more than 300 customers deployed it in under six months, and over 75% were already running it in production blocking mode. The preview mentioned AI-security customer growth but had not anticipated these deployment and production figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total security revenue grew 10% to approximately $1.3 billion (product security up 15% to $746 million), and over 300 customers deployed AI-powered WAF in under six months with more than 75% running in production blocking mode.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “AI security customer count” had doubled in Q3, but did not cite security-revenue or AI-WAF deployment expectations.
